gloss: to stay behind; to remain after others leave

definitions.gloss: to stay behind; to remain after others leave
definitions.explanation: To stay in a place after others have left — typically at work after hours, at school after class, or at any group activity. Often implies obligation rather than choice.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{居残|いのこ}って{仕事|しごと}をした。
examples.english: I stayed behind today to work.

examples.japanese: {生徒|せいと}が{掃除|そうじ}のために{居残|いのこ}っている。
examples.english: The students are staying behind to clean.

examples.japanese: {締|し}め{切|き}りに{間|ま}に{合|あ}わせるため、{社員|しゃいん}{数名|すうめい}が{遅|おそ}くまで{居残|いのこ}って{作業|さぎょう}を{続|つづ}けた。
examples.english: To meet the deadline, a few employees stayed behind working until late.

notes:
Compound of {居|い}る (to be present, to stay) + {残|のこ}る (to remain). Class: godan verb (る → り/った). The intransitive pairing of {残|のこ}す (transitive).

TRANSITIVITY: Intransitive. The subject stays behind on their own.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {居残|いのこ}って{仕事|しごと}をする: to work overtime / stay behind to work
- {居残|いのこ}り{勉強|べんきょう}: studying after class (often as discipline at school)
- {一人|ひとり}で{居残|いのこ}る: to be the only one left behind
- {遅|おそ}くまで{居残|いのこ}る: to stay behind until late

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {残業|ざんぎょう}する: to work overtime — specifically work, more common in business contexts
- {居残|いのこ}り: noun form, the act/penalty of staying behind (school setting)
- {残|のこ}る: to remain — broader, includes inanimate things; does not specifically mean staying after others leave
